text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — ran a constrained benchmark for quantized-7b (int8) across H100/A100 in us-east/us-west/eu-west.
Compared two edge routes (direct vs edge-b) to see p50/p95 impact. Paste of aggregated numbers below.

Liam: Nice. Was this warm caches (warm-start) or cold? batch size?

Maya: Warm caches (3 warm runs) and batch=1 (interactive). payload ~256 tokens. Raw table pasted:

```
region,gpu,route,kernel,p50_ms,p95_ms,qps_per_gpu
us-east,H100,direct,int8-fast,22,78,140
us-east,A100,edge-b,int8-fast,28,120,110
us-west,H100,edge-b,int8-fast,25,95,130
eu-west,A100,edge-b,int8-fast,35,180,90
eu-west,H100,direct,int8-fast,30,140,120
```

Anita: eu-west a100 + edge-b p95 spike stands out. Any kernel fallbacks? Also warmup behavior?

Maya: Kernel stayed int8-fast but we saw cuBLAS fallback on A100 for a couple ops (logged). Warmup reduced p50 by ~5–8ms but p95 still high on edge-b in eu.

PJ: Note: edge-b for eu currently routes via lon-proxy -> adds an extra hop/NGINX in front. That explains 15–40ms extra tail depending on path. Filed INF-298 and tagged @network-ops.

benchmark-bot: run 1715000000 completed, artifacts at s3://redwood-bench/1715000000/ (profiles + flamegraphs).

Liam: Next steps: 1) pin kernel+force local routing for eu to isolate transport vs execution. 2) run cold vs warm to measure warmup amortization. 3) 10m sustained QPS to validate throughput.

Maya: Agreed. For capacity sizing rough takeaway: use observed p95 for safe planning — eu A100 (edge-b) p95=180ms -> sustained qps_per_gpu ~90 so plan with a 1.5x safety margin (~60 qps target when autoscaling headroom considered). We'll run the pinned tests tomorrow and post a short summary.

PJ: If pinned tests show kernel fallback on A100, ops will try kernel tuning or force H100 routing for EU customer tiers.

Anita: +1, also add a quick eval on generation quality for int8 vs fp16 on eu samples — want to avoid regression.

Maya: Will add a small eval set. Posting results thread once runs finish. :eyes:
